html:<b>舞台右上角那个小窗</b>是同一套东西的实时版：把 3D 世界从:
html:The small window at the top right of the stage is the real-time version of the same thing: the 3D world is rendered again from the position of the fly's eyes (each eye turned 50° towards the front) and imaged through the same sampling table. To run in real time it skips flyvis and the decoder, stopping at "what the retina receives". It used to refresh only 3 times per second, because a synchronous GPU pixel readback waits for a round trip of about 4–5 ms; measurement showed that stall does not depend at all on how many faces are read, how many pixels, or how large the texture is (reading 1 face 6.3 ms ≈ reading 6 faces 6.8 ms; edge length 192→48 is no cheaper), so lowering the resolution does not help. After switching to WebGL2 PBO asynchronous readback (data collected on the next frame, verified byte-identical to the synchronous path), a single read dropped from 10.6 ms to 2.9 ms; it now measures 23 fps, with the main view still at 60 fps.
The "Dodge by eyes only" toggle replaces the game's visual front end: normally the fly reads the ball's world coordinates directly to compute the rate of angular expansion (a hand-written rule that looks only at the ball and ignores everything else in the scene); with it on, the fly can rely only on the readings of these 721 ommatidia — real pixels → Rh1 (R1–R6) → flyvis → T4/T5 pooled away from the centre in the form of Klapoetke et al. 2017 → LC4/LPLC2. The result is negative, and measurable: the ball has a radius of 2.5 mm and the interommatidial angle is 5.7°, so beyond 60 mm the ball covers less than one ommatidium; measured, this real vision is completely blind beyond 45 mm (the reading is constantly 0) and only separates the ball from the noise within 25 mm, whereas the hand-written front end tracks it from 110 mm. Worse, just by walking, the whole-field optic flow of the fly's self-motion creates spurious "looming" peaking at 126 Hz — so with it on the fly scares itself into taking off as it walks. This is not the model being broken; it is the problem that real flies cancel with their antennae and halteres, and this model has neither. The toggle is off by default, and turning it on costs frame rate (about 12 ms each time). During rendering the fly's own mesh is hidden — the camera sits in front of the body, and otherwise its own head would smear across half the field of view.
Each photoreceptor class integrates over its own spectrum: this used to be a Bayer-like approximation ("pale ommatidia take the blue channel, yellow take the green"); now, using the visual-pigment template of Govardovskii et al. 2000, each receptor's weights on the three rendered bands (UV 300–400, blue 400–500, green 500–700) are integrated in 1 nm steps from its own λmax: Rh3 (R7p, 345nm) gets 99.8% from UV, Rh4 (R7y, 375nm) 88.3%, Rh5 (R8p, 437nm) 66.4% blue, Rh6 (R8y, 508nm) 43.4% green. More importantly, Rh1 (R1–R6) has been added — six of the eight photoreceptors, the main channel for motion and brightness, which was previously not modelled at all, and which is precisely flyvis's main input. Two assumptions must be stated: the scene is authored in sRGB with no real spectra, so the three channels are treated as the mean reflectance of each band; and fly R1–6 also have a 3-hydroxyretinol sensitising pigment that gives a second peak at ~350nm, which is not in the template, so it is added here with a hand-picked amplitude (both sets of weights are in results/vision/opsin_weights.json for comparison).
The edge of the visual field is no longer approximate: at first we used perspective projection + FlyGym's fisheye correction, but perspective projection inherently cannot reach 180°; at 157° the edge was already stretched extremely flat, and the fisheye formula also has a singularity. It now uses a cube map — six 90° faces covering the whole sphere, with each ommatidium sampled exactly along its own line of sight, needing no distortion compensation. Ommatidial directions are defined on a hexagonal lattice: radius 15, interommatidial angle 5.7°, 171° field of view per eye, close to the real fly (literature ~160–180°). Measured in a geometry self-check: mean error 0.7° over 9 known directions.
The ultraviolet (R7) channel is a hand-written setting: there is no UV in an sRGB render, so each class of object in the scene was assigned a UV reflectance. The basis is the real structure of the UV world — in nature the sky is by far the dominant UV source and most surfaces are very dark in UV, and flies use exactly this contrast to find open space and tell up from down. But the values have no measured basis at all; they are only structurally plausible, and uploaded photos contain no UV information whatsoever.
Why it looks all green: at first the whole court used the page's theme colour (floor #1a211e), where the green and blue channels differ by only 11%, so to the fly's eye there was effectively no colour; on top of that, each ommatidium measures only one channel and the image is coloured by receptor type, and 70% are the yellow type → 70% of the cells are inherently green. The court now uses realistic colours (wooden floor, white lines, blue and red seats) and applies demosaicing — filling in each ommatidium's missing channel with the average of neighbours of the other type, the same thing a Bayer filter does (the fly itself does not get both channels at every ommatidium; this is interpolation for display, and can be switched off to see the raw mosaic).
Measured after the change: scene G/B went from 36.6/32.5 to 76/49, in-eye G/B = 0.310/0.205, and 41 ommatidia lean blue (the blue seats). But overall it is still greenish, and that is correct — the wooden floor is orange, and the fly has no red receptor, so orange stimulates only its green channel and barely touches the blue one. To a fly, the basketball court is a sheet of dark green.
Still approximate: the interommatidial angle is a constant 5.7° (in real flies it varies from ~4.5° at the front to ~8° at the side); the sky is the game's CSS gradient and not in the 3D scene, so the off-screen render fills the background with the stage sky colour.
html:<b>我们和它们的差别，只有一条，但是这条最贵</b>：这个页面里<b: html:There is only one difference between us and them, but it is the most expensive one: this page has no trained readout layer anywhere. From LC4/LPLC2 to the giant fibre, from sugar receptors to MN9, from JO to aDN1, everything in between is real synapses from the connectome, and the parameters are the paper's LIF set. The price is that it is dumb — dodging balls relies on a hand-written dθ/dt front end, and when it really has to see with pixels alone it is completely blind beyond 45 mm (we turned that negative result into a toggle too). What we get in return is the ability to run controls: the "Prove the connectome really matters" mission in mission mode is exactly scrambling the wiring and watching it collapse. The paper's Supplementary Table 1D does the same thing; we measured sugar → MN9 dropping from 82.9 Hz to 3.5 Hz.
html:两个阶段。<b>阶段一</b>：把「落子评分算法」当训练数据——让读出: html:Two stages. Stage one: the "move-scoring algorithm" is used as training data — the readout is fitted to the teacher's log scores for all line patterns (only 6,266 of them ever appear in the training positions; with move labels alone the values of the rest drift freely, and the search collapses as soon as it enters an unseen position). Stage two: fine-tuning on the best moves from depth-8 search (). Chart, left: the fly has never seen categories such as "open three" or "four"; the categories are used only to group the learned values — see whether the order it arrives at by itself is right. Right: validation agreement during stage two as a function of training steps, starting from the stage-one score.
html:<span class=\"tag c\">连接组 · 半</span: html:Connectome · halfThe "what is the fly thinking" bubble: the quantities that trigger each word are real — sweet / bitter / wind / itch are the current frequencies injected into those sensory neurons, and eat / groom / back up / fly are the smoothed firing rates of the readout neurons; but the word thresholds and the Chinese sentence templates are hand-written. This is a simplified version of section 13 of the report: there, 121,706 neurons + ridge regression decode 12 words; here the sub-circuit has only 4,599 neurons and none of the vinegar / mould / temperature and humidity pathways, so it can only use the few inputs that really exist in the game, with thresholds instead of regression.
html:世界自己运转：昼夜、烂果子和水洼、气味、嗡嗡声、热源、风、灰尘、偶尔飞: html:The world runs on its own: day and night, rotting fruit and puddles, odours, buzzing, heat sources, wind, dust, the occasional incoming ball. Each is delivered only as physical quantities to real receptors (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch, plus temperature and humidity); where to turn, whether to fly, whether to eat — all of it is decided by this connectome of neurons — there is not a single "smell it, go to it" or "hear it, run" rule. It has a mushroom body: when an odour and dopamine occur together, the corresponding synapses are depressed — it remembers. Its body is pushed along by six legs; you can amputate legs, or hold a button to remote-control a few neurons directly.
html:<b>一个必须说明的限制</b>：flyvis 自带 <b>50 个<: html:A limitation that must be stated: flyvis ships 50 pretrained ensemble members — under connectome constraints the solution is not unique, and the authors themselves stress the differences between members. We use one of them (flow/0000/000). After running all 50: "the whole network is a hexagonal convolution" holds 50/50; but the preferred directions of the T4/T5 subtypes scatter widely between members, and several visual conclusions we drew from member 000 cannot be taken as general properties of flyvis (see report §33).
html:<span class=\"tag h\">手写</span>进食/梳: html:Hand-writtenFeeding/grooming/backing up: pellet under the head → sugar/bitter 200 Hz; dust on an antenna → that side's JO 200 Hz; LC16 = 0.5 Hz/(°/s) × angular velocity; thresholds MN9 30 Hz, aDN1 20 Hz, MDN 20 Hz; priority takeoff > backing up > feeding > grooming > walking. Proboscis extension is a purely visual rotation of the proboscis mesh; the grooming pose is generated by inverse kinematics bringing the foreleg tips to the antennae (after the foreleg grooming type in the flybody grooming pose dataset).

So the chain "wind → these neurons fire → downstream readout" is computed by the connectome; the conversion from wind speed to firing frequency, the geometry of the antennae facing the wind, and the force with which the wind pushes the fly off course are all hand-written (there is no calibration data for this model).

You can switch back to the first version (both use dθ/dt).

html:三因子规则，只改读出层：Δw = 学习率 × <b>δ</b> × 资: html:A three-factor rule that changes only the readout: Δw = learning rate × δ × eligibility trace, δ = this game's result − recent average = reward prediction error, which corresponds to the dopamine signal in reinforcement learning. To be clear: this model's own dopaminergic neurons do not fire at all outside runaway conditions (PAM 0/307), so δ is computed outside the connectome. html:学到的是什么：碰到水就停下来喝（水味先天只把 MN9 推到十几 Hz，: html:What is learned: stop and drink on touching water (water taste innately pushes MN9 only to a dozen or so Hz, not enough for proboscis extension), and turn less when humidity rises. Not learned: finding water from a distance: {8} s vs {9} s in the drought world, and training longer changes nothing (30 lives {10} s, 120 lives {11} s). The arm that cannot see the brain's output learns just as well — in this task the connectome provides the body and the reflexes, not the learning signal.
html:有人看到果蝇走到场边会一直顶着围栏往前走。查下来<b>不是它认不出墙<: html:Someone noticed that when the fly reaches the edge of the court it keeps pushing forward against the fence. It turned out not to be that it cannot recognise the wall: the court boundary is just a geometric clamp at the end of each step, and the hand-written visual front end reads only the ball's world coordinates to compute the rate of angular expansion, ignoring everything else in the scene. Measured (no ball, 120 s × 3 seeds): 92.8% of the time against the wall, the longest continuous stretch 111 s.

html:无人值守。你不给果蝇下任务——你只设计这个箱子的规则，然后看它在生存压: html:Unattended. You do not give the fly tasks — you only design the rules of this box, then watch it learn and evolve on its own under the pressure to survive. The connectome is the fixed body; the plastic layer is learning during life, and reward comes only from its own body: when it eats, it gets a little less hungry. You cannot change the reward, only the world. ← Back to Digital Fly Lab

Five orders of magnitude apart — the low resolution is not crude simulation; it is the world as a fly sees it.
